s1.syndrome_frame: a chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesion with erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels with plump endothelial cells
positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34
key_facts: female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
lesions located on left upper arm and left side of chest
no triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma
no fever, weight loss, or fatigue
multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders
histopathological examination showed thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels
endothelial cells were plump with no significant cytologic atypia
immunohistochemistry positive for CD31, CD34, and Ki-67 (<1%)
immunohistochemistry negative for podoplanin (D2-40) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

shortlist.label: epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders and histopathological findings of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels

shortlist.label: microvenular hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the patient's age and sex, and histopathological features of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels

shortlist.label: tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: possible diagnosis given the clinical presentation of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques

shortlist.label: targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, although less likely than epithelioid hemangioma

shortlist.label: morpheaform hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: a possible diagnosis given the clinical presentation and histopathological findings, although less common than epithelioid hemangioma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders, along with the histopathological findings of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles, is most consistent with morpheaform hemangioma.

rejected.label: epithelioid hemangioma
rejected.why: Epithelioid hemangioma typically presents with more distinct epithelioid endothelial cells and a greater degree of cellular atypia, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: microvenular hemangioma
rejected.why: Microvenular hemangioma is characterized by small, thin-walled vessels, but it typically lacks the thickened collagen bundles seen in this patient's histopathology.

rejected.label: tufted angioma
rejected.why: Tufted angioma is typically associated with a more distinct tufted or cannonball pattern of vascular proliferation, which is not evident in this case.

rejected.label: targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma is characterized by a distinctive targetoid appearance and hemosiderin deposition, neither of which is present in this patient's presentation.
